This vignette provides an introduction how to use the ParlAT package in order to the access and subseqently analyze the Open Data provided by the Austrian Parliament.

Get mandates

Get the mandates of one or more individuals. Each row in the returned tibble represents data on one specific mandate.

get_mandates(names=c("Kogler Werner", "Nehammer Karl", "Götze Elisabeth", "Beck Pia Philippa", "Strache Pia Philippa"), institution = "all")

Get names 

get_names(44127, date="01/01/2024")
#>   index pad_intern              name date_start date_end        name_clean name_family    name_given value
#> 1     1      44127 Pia Philippa Beck 2023-06-28     <NA> Pia Philippa Beck        Beck Pia Philippa   <NA>
get_names(44127, date="01/01/2023")
#>   index pad_intern                 name date_start   date_end           name_clean name_family    name_given                                 value
#> 1     1      44127 Pia Philippa Strache       <NA> 2023-06-27 Pia Philippa Strache     Strache Pia Philippa  (bis 27.6.2023: Pia Philippa Strache)
get_pad_intern("Strache")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   pad_intern names_variants                         
#>   <chr>      <chr>                                  
#> 1 1905       Max Strache                            
#> 2 35518      Heinz-Christian Strache                
#> 3 44127      Pia Philippa Beck, Pia Philippa Strache

Get MPs

Get all female MPs of the FPÖ.

Note the importance of the make_unique argument. By default, the API of the Parliament returns a row fo each unqiue MP name. However, since MPs can change their name, a standard query returns multiple rows for the same MP. The make_unique argument takes care of this duplications and returns only one row per MP identifier (pad_intern) and returns the different name variants as a list.


df <- get_mps(institution="NR", party = "FPÖ", gender="female", echo=FALSE)
class(df)
names(df)

class(df$pad_intern)
df %>% dplyr::filter(pad_intern==41)
